newsitem.title: CANADA: Loewen sees '97 revenue at US$1.2 bln.
newsitem.headline: Loewen sees '97 revenue at US$1.2 bln.

text.p: Canadian funeral home operator Loewen Group Inc said on Thursday it expected revenues to climb to US$1.2 billion in 1997, up from US$908.4 million in 1996.
"Our...annualized revenues have grown from US$21 million in 1987 to an estimated US$1.2 billion for 1997," chief executive Ray Loewen told the company's annual meeting.
Speaking later to reporters, he clarified that this 1997 figure was a consensus estimate from analysts and said the company agreed with the projections.
Loewen executives said analysts expect US$100 million in earnings this year or earnings per share of US$1.55 to US$1.60.
"We agree with analysts' expectations," Ray Loewen said.
He said the fast-growing company had signed or closed US$515 million worth of acquisitions so far in 1997 with an average return on investment estimated at 16.4 percent.

The company had projected its acquisitions would total US$600 million for the year. Loewen said that estimate was not being officially revised but that "it now looks like we are going to pass that US$600 million."

Loewen fought off a hostile takeover bid from arch-rival Service Corp International earlier this year and the two often compete to acquire independent funeral homes and cemeteries as the "death care" industry rapidly consolidates.
The field remains wide open for acquisitions, Loewen said. He estimated only 10 percent of a North American industry valued at US$50 billion is in the hands of the major firms.
Loewen said the company's strong acquisitions record helped make it one of the world's 200 fastest growing companies.

Noting a recent upgrade in the company's credit rating, he said it was just a matter of time before Loewen regains an investment grade rating. It was downgraded after narrowly averting bankruptcy in 1995 over a Mississippi court case.
Since that case and the Service Corp takeover battle, Loewen struggled to regain credibility with shareholders and boost its share price. Ray Loewen said the company was now back on track.

Loewen executives are currently meeting with institutional investors about an offering of 10 million shares that is expected to raise US$300 million to US$350 million. The offering will be priced the week of May 26.
Loewen's banks have offered to increase the company's revolving line of credit to US$1 billion from US$750 million when the share issue is completed.
